title: Listing of Foreign Organisations That May Pose Security Concerns and Advisory for Citizens Volunteering Overseas
what_it_is: Listing of Foreign Organisations That May Pose Security Concerns and Advisory for Citizens Volunteering Overseas

sections.label: Foreign organisations and security laws
sections.summary: The passage states designated terrorist entities are listed in the Terrorism (Suppression of Financing) Act and no broader public list is planned.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: For example, certain foreign organisations designated as terrorist entities are listed in the First Schedule to the Terrorism (Suppression of Financing) Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: There are no plans to make public a broader list of foreign organisations that may pose concerns to Singapore's national security.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Such a list may give rise to operational and security risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Regular publicity and outreach efforts are conducted to raise public awareness of security threats, including from foreign organisations of concern such as foreign terrorist groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We have also publicly stated that Singaporeans should not participate in foreign armed conflicts, and should exercise particular care in dealing with organisations with links to foreign militaries or foreign security and intelligence agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: There are also restrictions and responsibilities under various statutes such as the Foreign Interference (Countermeasures) Act, in relation to membership in a foreign legislature or foreign political organisation, or the United Nations Act which includes prohibitions against providing technical advice, assistance or training to designated foreign persons, entities and organisations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Where necessary, the Government will issue travel advisories on overseas developments that may have security implications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Singaporeans should exercise due diligence and err on the side of caution when in doubt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: It is ultimately every individual's responsibility to ensure that they comply with our laws and not act in a manner prejudicial to Singapore’s national interest.

sections.label: Disseminating information on security risks
sections.summary: The passage states information is disseminated so Singaporeans are aware of security risks and grasp national interests.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: This is one way through which we disseminate important information so that Singaporeans are aware of security risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Also, when there are cases that the Member Ms Hazlina has raised, we have also amplified existing messages through the media and ultimately, it is very important for Singaporeans to have a good grasp of what our national interests are.
